We present a randomized controlled trial evaluating the effect of a twelve-week interval training program on cardiorespiratory fitness in adults with sedentary occupations. Participants were allocated to either a supervised exercise group or a usual-care control group. Primary outcome was change in peak oxygen uptake measured by maximal exercise testing. Secondary outcomes included resting blood pressure and self-reported quality of life. Results showed a statistically significant improvement in the intervention arm, with no serious adverse events reported.
